column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3b store, the yardstick behind row 12 (Blackbaud: 5% of confirmed assets over five years, quote rechecked at source today); a software default, never the profession's law (rows 8-9).
Mon 16 Nov: the same 5% rule from the same publisher; its income line (5-10% of annual income) adds nothing a part needs.

Mon 16 Nov: store, the textbook's age table; rightly claims no band for Laura (the case gives only her 2018 graduation, l.16); read only through a handout, so cite the handout or read Hogan before use.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store, the most generous yardstick (fully commits, 10% over 3-5 years) still sits far below $115,000 of the $450,000 she puts in; a 2017 vendor glossary, recheck before citing.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; drop the gloss that 10% of a year's income is the same five-year rule written another way: income and net worth are different bases.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store, capacity is a donor's whole budget to all causes, never one organisation's ask, which is why row 12 is a yardstick, not an expectation.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store, the five years is a pledge-instalment convention; Laura's contribution is one payment from money owned before she states it, a contrast co-sponsors would recognise.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b guard, the 5% rule began as an income ratio and its own profession calls it a myth, so any yardstick clause says rule of thumb and is held lightly; the IRS 2008 data behind it not checked.
Mon 16 Nov: wording guard for 3b: never fundraisers would rate her as if one rule existed; at most by the common rule of thumb.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; one campaign quoted in a comment, data unseen; drop the comparison of 25.6% of deposits with a net-worth rating, or carry row 12's caveat (case l.61-63).

Mon 16 Nov: 3b, for a founder inclination is total and readiness is set by the case's dates, so only capacity is left to judge and the plan answers it by owning first; Keel inference on Apra's definition.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b, answers timid, generous or reckless in one dollar clause (the common 5% rule expects $115,000 over five years from someone worth about $2.3 million); 25.6%, 5.1 times, 2.6 times and $2.3m / $1.15m / $11.5m reproduce from NUMBERS 4 and Q32-035; never imply the $450,000 is her wealth (case l.61-63) and hold the rule lightly (rows 8-9).

Mon 16 Nov: 3b; $514,357 and 87.6% reproduce (NUMBERS 8k, of the deposits grown to $587,141), but add the caveat its disanalogy column lacks: the rules rate general wealth and her portfolio is a dedicated fund (case l.61-63), so no rule was meant for it; name the base, since SKELETON 3b uses 8k's other figure (87.2% of all the money at the end); keep the aha, safe by owning first, not by smallness.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b, a leading philanthropy scholar refuses any fixed share: responsible giving is the donor's own judgement on her own goals, which the IPS's order expresses; an interview, not research.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b, the private bank's definition of responsible giving (needs first at high confidence, give from what is left) answers the case's word responsibly (l.101-105) with the IPS's own order; the 95% stays here, never on 3c (Q71, Q74).

Mon 16 Nov: 3a or 3b; fix a private bank calls a lifestyle secured at 1 in 20, which reads backwards: say Bernstein sizes core capital to last in 19 of 20 simulated markets while none of Laura's payments depends on a share price (quote IPS l.11 exactly); a simulation test and an ownership test stay different kinds of claim.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.0 and 3b support for row 18: UBS funds a liquidity ladder first and calls only what is left legacy; its ladder covers 2-5 years of spending, Laura's ten.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.0 and 3b, the aha: wealth managers invest the giving bucket aggressively because it has no date (UBS 2024, quotes rechecked at source today), and Laura's plan agrees only until a figure gets a date and a listener, then half moves into Treasuries (IPS l.11, l.15); the floor is in Treasuries from 2028, so say shares hold only money not yet promised, never that all the facility money waits in shares.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b or 3f, a bank's words for TNA note 3's own thought (VT is where we allow ourselves to be wrong), showing the team's reasoning matches practice; a marketing document.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b or 3c store, Murphy's permanent difference as what the 2031 move makes of the building money; read only in Schervish's quotation, so cite it as quoted there or read Murphy (2001) first.
Mon 16 Nov: store, discernment begins with capacity; a generic process frame the IPS's order already shows.
Mon 16 Nov: store, the very rich keep more than they need; the 67% only with the report says (its medians do not reconcile), and lifestyle security is not Laura's question (case l.61-63).
Mon 16 Nov: store, an aggregate finding on giving and economic security; owning first as security is Keel's stretch, one clause at most.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b and 3e, the gift planners' code asks that consequences for the donor be apparent and illustrations realistic, the test 3e meets with dated assumptions (7.5% in the upper third of fifteen houses, CANON B15); a conduct code, not a size rule.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store, the UK hardship test; the case already settles it (living costs outside the portfolio, l.61-63), so it confirms rather than argues; written for vulnerable donors.
Mon 16 Nov: the same point as row 25 (a gift must not harm the giver) from a weaker source; the case's l.102-103 already says it.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; about research conduct and privacy, not gift size, by its own disanalogy, so it serves no part.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b scale only, the wealthy give a fraction of 1% of net worth a year (1995 SCF); never set her dedicated fund against a fortune as like for like.
Mon 16 Nov: the same scale point on a skewed 2022 sample; 0.1% reproduces (34,917 of 31 million) but adds nothing to row 28.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c or 3d contrast, the best-known big promise is a share of future wealth, moral not legal and undated, against Laura's dated dollar figures owned first; pairs with Q52-029 (8 of 22 kept); never compare fortunes.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, another pledge's share of income; no part needs it.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, UNVERIFIED (read in Candid's summary of a paid report); serves no part.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b, the case asks how much of the remaining portfolio she can responsibly contribute (l.101-102), and centrally it is about four-fifths: $115,000 of $144,823, 79.4%, reproduces from NUMBERS 4; central only, and SKELETON 3b's figure stays $115,000 of the $450,000, so one share figure at most.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b; 20.6% and 5.1% reproduce only for $29,823, her flexibility plus anything above the top (NUMBERS 4, 8k); half the shares alone ($21,347) is 3.6% of the $589,655, so half of the shares is about five cents of every dollar (this row's use and Claim 4's judge's note) must read about 3.6 cents, or about 5 cents with anything above the top, said so (WORDS).
Mon 16 Nov: store, keeping back is built into the gift annuity (a 50% residuum target); never as a reason for IPS l.15's half, which Caplet chose (NUMBERS 8o).
Mon 16 Nov: store, donors value timing flexibility even for money already given; a behaviour parallel only, since DAF money is irrevocable (Q18 r31).

Mon 16 Nov: 3b store, half of wealthy donors find it hard to know what they can afford to give, the case's own question (l.101-102), which the plan answers with a rule and an owned figure; executive summary only.
Mon 16 Nov: store, advisers misread why the wealthy hold back; that her flexibility serves the project's risks is IPS l.15's own point, so this adds colour only.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the case already puts her needs outside the portfolio (l.61-63).

Mon 16 Nov: 3d store, small online donors' figures move with their finances while after the move Laura's is certain (NUMBERS 4); co-sponsors are foundations and firms, so a loose parallel, with Q50's can.
Mon 16 Nov: restates the store and SKELETON 3b (case l.102-103 in H7-085 and H9-024, 8o's $5,300 per $5,000 in Q43-016, IPS l.15's three uses); its figures reproduce.
